verdict.rationale: Smithery documents plugging in arbitrary MCP servers as connections, both via its REST connect interface and via `smithery mcp add <url>`, including local servers through Uplink. It then lists and calls their tools directly (`smithery tool call`) or aggregates tools from multiple servers for agent SDKs, while handling OAuth and token refresh. missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration that adding and calling tools works as documented, and evidence that Smithery itself orchestrates tool use rather than only brokering connections and calls for downstream agents.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can plug MCP servers into this product so it can use their tools

citations.quote: Smithery gives you a simple REST interface for connecting to MCP servers.
smithery mcp add <url>                  # Add an MCP server connection
smithery tool call <connection> <tool> [args]  # Call a tool
Connect to multiple servers and aggregate their tools
Uplink exposes an MCP server running on any machine as a regular Smithery connection.
